Definition: to braid, i.e. intermix; technically, to traffic (as if by barter); also or give to be security (as a kind of exchange)
BiblicalUsage: The word means to give a pledge, to stand surety for another, and it runs through the whole Bible. Judah becomes surety for Benjamin, the Proverbs warn against becoming surety for a friend or striking hands for a stranger, and Job asks God to put him in surety with Himself, since no one else will strike hands for him.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe surety is the shape of love that puts its own name on the line. Judah did it for Benjamin, and Christ did it for us, standing surety where no one else could.
